subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should isolated cron jobs get a first-class `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` policy, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or continue with only per-job `payload.toolsAllow` plus delivery safeguards?
rationale: The choice defines a scheduled-run tool-access boundary and public config contract, including whether existing jobs that directly use `message` under announce delivery keep working by default.

options.title: Add Cron-Scoped Policy
options.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with explicit precedence and tests for `message` denial across cron delivery modes.

options.title: Inherit Subagent Policy
options.body: Apply `tools.subagents.tools` to cron sessions too, reducing config surface but coupling two different execution modes.

options.title: Keep Per-Job Only
options.body: Avoid a new global cron policy and rely on `payload.toolsAllow`, docs, and delivery safeguards for scheduled runs.

recommendation.title: Add Cron-Scoped Policy
recommendation.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with explicit precedence and tests for `message` denial across cron delivery modes.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined signal from prior review context plus recent cron runner and scoped tool-policy foundation work.
